Subject: Question about DSR delete and month-end invoices

Hi Hannah,

Hope you’re well — quick question on behalf of our finance team. We have an upcoming audit and one of the auditors asked whether a customer Data Subject Request (DSR) to delete a user would also remove the underlying usage records or invoice line items that we rely on for month-end reconciliation.

Specifics: we need to know whether Redwood preserves invoices and usage ledgers separately from any content-level deletions, and whether you can provide a short explanation or evidence we can show to our auditors. We attached our PO for July for context (Centauri_PO_202607.pdf).

Two asks:
- Can you confirm if invoices and billing ledgers remain available after a user/account-level deletion request?
- If yes, can you provide the format and retention window (e.g., how many years) and whether those records contain any user-identifying personal data?

Thanks — we’re aiming to close the reconciliation question today, so any quick guidance would be very helpful.

Best,
Elena Morris
Head of Finance, Centauri Analytics
elena@centauri.com

Subject: Re: Question about DSR delete and month-end invoices

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the PO. Looping in Finance (Neha) and Product Ops (Aditya) for the precise artifacts, but short answer up front: invoices and the accounting/usage ledger are treated as accounting records and are preserved for reconciliation/audit purposes even if a separate DSR requests deletion of user-generated content.

High-level points:
- Billing records (invoice PDFs, aggregated usage ledgers, and transaction metadata) are retained to satisfy accounting, tax, and audit obligations. We do not delete these artifacts as part of a standard DSR erasure that targets user content.
- Invoices and ledgers are considered system-of-record financial artifacts; they are retained separately from user content stores and are accessible to the customer via the Console/exports or by request.
- Sensitive personal data is minimized on invoices: line items are usage aggregates (tokens/units per invoice period) and typically do not include conversational content. If a customer requests further redaction of PII, we can produce a redacted export for audit review.

I’ve attached a short internal summary of our accounting retention policy for invoices (Acct_Policy_Summary.pdf) and included a link to the guidance doc for auditors. Neha — can you confirm the retention window that Finance cites for audit purposes and whether we can provide a signed letter for Centauri’s auditors? Aditya — can you confirm the exact export format for the ledger (CSV columns) so Elena can confirm it will match Centauri’s reconciliation import?

Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks for raising — I’m Neha from Finance. A few concrete items to help your auditors:

1) Retention window: Redwood retains invoice PDFs and the internal billing ledger for a minimum of 7 years for accounting and audit compliance. This is our baseline; where local laws require longer retention we follow those requirements.

2) What’s stored: the billing ledger contains aggregated usage metrics (date range, product SKU, quantity, amount, invoice id, customer account id). We treat conversational content and user-provided content separately and do not keep full conversation text in the billing ledger. Billing artifacts may include an account identifier that is customer-owned (account id) and possibly the billing contact email; they do not include message bodies.

3) Deletion interplay: a DSAR that triggers erasure of user content will not automatically remove invoice PDFs or ledger line items. If a customer requests further redaction of PII inside billing artifacts, we can provide a redacted export.

4) Evidence for auditors: we can provide:
   - Official letter confirming our retention policy (signed by Finance)
   - A CSV export of the billing ledger for the requested period with optional redaction
   - An invoice PDF bundle for the relevant months

I’m attaching a month-end reconciliation checklist that shows the ledger columns and a suggested ingestion mapping (month_end_recon_checklist.xlsx). We can put together a short signed statement next business day — please confirm the exact month(s) you need (July 2026?) and whether you require redaction of billing contact emails.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
